headline: Harvard gave prisoners psilocybin to stop them reoffending.
slides: Timothy Leary's Harvard team ran an experiment at Concord prison in Massachusetts.
32 inmates took psilocybin in group therapy sessions, two to five times each.
Leary reported far fewer of them went back to prison.
Rick Doblin re-checked the records 34 years later.
The claimed effect didn't hold up. The comparison had been flawed.
Doblin's conclusion: the sessions might help, but only with support after release.
sources: Sources: Doblin, 'Dr. Leary's Concord Prison Experiment: A 34-Year Follow-Up' (J. Psychoactive Drugs, 1998)
